<margin>Enemies are to be loved.</margin>
If he compels you to go one mile, go with him two. Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute and slander you, so that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven, who makes his sun rise on the good and the evil and rains on the just and the unjust. You respond, "He did not say this to me. He said it to the apostles, he said it to the perfect." Have you not heard, "so that you may be children of your Father"? If you do not desire to be a child of God, the law does not concern you. Although, not even a good person is someone who does not wish to be perfect. Accept that also; if you do not desire a reward, the commandment does not concern you. For it follows: "For if you love those who love you, <margin>Luke 6</margin> what reward will you have?" As if to say, none. For it is not a virtue to do this, but it is a sin not to do it. Nothing is owed to either party when like is returned for like. Listen to <margin>Paul, consultant of the laws.</margin> Paul, the great consultant and interpreter of Christian laws. Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not <margin>Rom. 12</margin> curse. Repaying no one evil for evil. If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, living at peace with all men, not defending yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath. For it is written: "Vengeance is mine, and I will repay," says the <margin>Deuteronomy 32</margin> Lord. "But if your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink." For in doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good. What, then, will happen, you ask, if I nourish the insolence of another with my gentleness and, by enduring an old injury, invite a new one? If you can escape or drive away evil without your own harm, no one forbids you from doing so; but if not, beware of saying that it is easier to do evil than to suffer it. If you can, improve the situation, either by overwhelming them with benefits or by conquering them with meekness. If otherwise, it is better for one to perish than for both; it is better for you to grow rich in the profit of patience than for both of you to become evil through mutual retaliation of evil. Therefore, let this be the Christian decree: to compete with all through <margin>Decree of Christianity.</margin> love, meekness, and kindness, but to willingly yield in matters of contention, slander, insult, or injury, even to the lowest. But you say, "They are unworthy of kindness, unworthy of being yielded to." Yet you are worthy to act, and Christ is worthy, for whose grace it is done. "Neither do I wish to injure anyone," they say, "nor will I suffer myself to be injured." <summary>Erasmus instructs the Christian to transcend retaliation by embracing patience, forgiveness, and active kindness toward enemies, citing the teachings of Christ and Paul as the basis for this moral decree.</summary>
